title: ParkourNote — a research workspace for papers, notes, videos and writing
excerpt: ParkourNote imports papers, books, web pages, videos and recordings, transcribes and translates them, and keeps your notes and questions beside the page — in the browser, Chrome and on your phone.
content_html:
ParkourNote imports what you read — papers, books, web pages, videos, feeds and recordings — transcribes and translates it, and keeps your notes and questions next to the page. It runs in the browser, in Chrome's side panel and on your phone, and Claude, ChatGPT or Codex can read your library through it.

01Collect

Everything you read comes into one library

Library & Inbox

Imports wait in an Inbox with a suggested project

Paste an arXiv id or a link, drop in a file, or clip a page from Chrome. New items land in the Inbox, and ParkourNote suggests where each one belongs and says why.

  • Papers from arXiv or any PDF, with title, authors and abstract attached. EPUB books, Markdown, web pages, YouTube and Bilibili videos, MP4 files, recordings, and Typst or LaTeX projects.
  • For each item the Inbox suggests a project, or a new project when nothing fits. Accept with Enter, pick another with 1–9, snooze it until tomorrow or next week, or archive it. The suggestion is only a suggestion; nothing moves until you say so.
  • Projects instead of folders. One item can sit in several projects, and deleting a project never deletes what's in it.
  • Duplicates are recognised across the library, and a PDF's own highlights and notes can come along on import.

Feeds

RSS, Atom and JSON feeds beside your papers

Subscribe to a journal, an arXiv category or a blog. Entries arrive in a feed tile and read in place.

  • Entries are listed newest first, with excerpts; open one and the full text reads in the tile.
  • A feed lives in a project, next to the papers it leads to.
  • Convert an entry into a document when it deserves highlights, translation or a question. Nothing is converted until you ask.
  • OPML import and export.

02Read

Read the original, the text and the translation side by side

The workspace

Papers, notes and chat tiled in one window

Everything in a project opens as a tile: readers, notes, feeds and the chat. Split them, stack them and drag them where you want them.

  • The layout belongs to the project and is still there tomorrow, on any computer you sign in from.
  • Project Home lists what's in progress, unopened, annotated or long, with reading progress and pins.
  • ⌘O opens any file, note, feed or project by name; ⌘⇧F searches the text, highlights and notes of a whole project.
  • Five themes from Paper to Dark, and separate text sizes for the interface, documents and chat.

The reader

Transcription and translation, block by block

Transcribe the pages you choose into an editable document, then translate it. Each block of text stays linked to its place on the page.

  • Transcription keeps headings, formulas, tables and figures. Long books split into one document per chapter.
  • Translation into eleven languages, shown under each block or in a second column beside the original, with maths and figures intact.
  • A contents dock built from the paper's own structure steers both the PDF and the document.
  • Select a word for a dictionary card — a built-in set plus MDX dictionaries you upload. Hover a link or citation on a PDF to see where it goes, and add a cited paper to the project in one click.

03Ask

Ask about the page you're on

The chat

A chat that has read the page with you

Every message carries what you can see: the visible pages, the passages you attached and the note in focus.

  • It reads other pages, searches your library, the web and arXiv, and opens a related paper for you.
  • Ask it to highlight something and the highlight is yours — anchored in the page and editable. Its answers cite pages you can click back to.
  • Attach a selection, box a figure or formula, paste a screenshot, or dictate your question.
  • Threads are kept per paper and per project, and all of them are in one list to pick back up.

Your own AI

Claude, ChatGPT and Codex can read your library

ParkourNote is also an MCP server. Connect Claude, Claude Code, ChatGPT or Codex once, and a conversation there can search your library, read papers and notes, and follow the page you have open.

How to connect
  • Sign in with OAuth — no API keys. You choose what it may do and can revoke it in Settings at any time.
  • Link a page with a one-time instruction: the AI sees the paper you're reading and can turn to another page or file for you.
  • It can search, read transcriptions and translations, list highlights, export citations, create notes and file papers into projects.
  • Every call it makes shows up in the chat tile as it happens, and you can pause the link at any time.

04Notes & writing

Take notes on anything, and write in the same place

Video notes

Notes pinned to the moment in a video

Paste a YouTube or Bilibili link or upload an MP4. The video opens as a tile, next to the papers it goes with.

  • Start typing and the time is pinned; a frame from the player comes with the note.
  • Each note carries a time chip that seeks the player back to that second.
  • Ask the chat about the video and it knows where you are and what is on screen.

Recordings

Record a meeting and get the minutes

Record from the browser or the phone. When you stop, the recording is transcribed and the minutes are written for you.

  • The recording uploads as you talk. Pause and continue as often as you like.
  • Every point in the minutes links to the moment it was said, playable in place.
  • Notes you type while recording are tied to the time you typed them.

Writing

Typst and LaTeX documents, compiled as you write

Start from a template or upload a .typ, a .tex or a whole project. The compiled pages open in the reader like any paper.

  • Click a line on the page and the source opens at that line; edit the source and the page recompiles.
  • Ask the chat for a change and it edits the source. Each change is a chip you can open to see the diff or revert.
  • Select a passage and press ⌘K to rewrite it in place, or say the change out loud. Tag versions and download the PDF.

05Everywhere

In Chrome and on your phone

Chrome extension

ParkourNote in Chrome's side panel

Open the side panel on any page to ask about it, clip it or import it. It uses the same account and library.

Get the extension
  • On arXiv or a publisher's page, import the paper. On any other page, clip it as an article, with a full snapshot if you want one.
  • On YouTube and Bilibili, take notes pinned to the time with a frame from the player, and ask about what's on screen.
  • Select text on any page and ask about it from the small ParkourNote pill.

iPhone & iPad

Your library on the phone

A native app for iPhone and iPad, currently in testing. It reads and edits the same library, and notes sync live with the browser.

About the apps
  • Read transcriptions with formulas rendered, and switch to the original pages when you need them.
  • Ask about the page from the bar at the bottom, by typing or by voice.
  • Edit notes in a native editor. Select text to ask, rewrite or translate it.
  • Record a meeting with the phone locked; the recording shows on the Lock Screen and the minutes are waiting when you stop.

  • Citations

    APA, MLA, Chicago, Harvard and IEEE. Cite a selection in one click; export BibTeX, BibLaTeX, RIS or CSL JSON.

  • Export

    Documents as Markdown with maths kept, rich text for Word, Pages or Notion, or the source as a zip — with translations if you like.

  • Search

    ⌘F inside a document, ⌘⇧F across a project, ⌘O to jump anywhere. Chinese, Japanese and Korean text is searchable too.

  • Dictionaries

    A built-in default set, plus MDX/MDD dictionaries you upload, shown with their original styling.

  • Eleven translation languages

    Chinese (simplified and traditional), English, Japanese, Korean, French, German, Spanish, Russian, Brazilian Portuguese and Indonesian.

  • Eleven interface languages

    English, 简体中文, 繁體中文, 日本語, 한국어, Español, Français, Deutsch, Português, Русский and Bahasa Indonesia — in the app, the extension and this site.

  • Themes and text size

    Light, Paper, Sepia, Dusk and Dark, or follow the system. Documents can keep a theme of their own.

  • Feedback that gets answered

    Press ⌘⇧M, mark up the frozen screen, and follow your report from received to fixed.
